skill.name: golang-pro
skill.description: Develop and review Go 1.21+ services using modern concurrency, testing, profiling, architecture, security, and production deployment practices.
skill.summary: Build maintainable, tested, and production-ready Go systems with expert guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive caused by benign guidance about simplicity and readability. No network reconnaissance instructions, prompt injection, or other malicious intent were found.

static_findings.snippet: - Emphasizes simplicity and readability over cleverness

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 136 only recommends simplicity and readability. It contains no network reconnaissance command, procedure, or request.

content.value_statement: Complex Go services require careful concurrency, architecture, testing, and performance decisions. This skill provides focused guidance for maintainable Go 1.21+ systems.
actual_capabilities: Designs goroutine, channel, worker pool, pipeline, cancellation, and graceful shutdown patterns.
Reviews Go architecture using interfaces, composition, clean architecture, and domain-driven design.
Guides CPU, memory, garbage collection, database, and network performance analysis.
Creates testing strategies with table-driven tests, benchmarks, mocks, integration tests, and coverage.
Advises on HTTP, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, database, caching, and authentication implementations.
Recommends container, Kubernetes, observability, logging, CI, and production readiness practices.
limitations: The skill targets Go 1.21+ and does not provide equivalent guidance for other languages.
Recommendations require validation against the actual repository, dependencies, runtime, and deployment environment.
Performance improvements require measurements from benchmarks, profiles, traces, or production telemetry.
Security and compliance decisions still require organization-specific review and testing.

use_cases.title: Learn Modern Go Patterns
use_cases.description: Understand idiomatic error handling, interfaces, generics, contexts, tests, and project organization through focused examples.
use_cases.target_user: Go developers expanding beyond basic syntax

use_cases.title: Review Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Evaluate service boundaries, persistence, APIs, observability, deployment, and operational reliability before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Performance
use_cases.description: Use benchmarks, profiles, traces, and concurrency analysis to identify measured improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Go Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain [Go concept] for a beginner. Include its purpose, a practical example, common mistakes, and a small testing strategy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learning an unfamiliar Go language or standard library feature

prompt_templates.title: Review Go Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go code for correctness, idioms, error handling, concurrency safety, and test gaps. Prioritize findings and explain each proposed change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving an existing package or pull request

prompt_templates.title: Design a Concurrent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Go [worker pool or pipeline] for [workload]. Address backpressure, cancellation, error propagation, shutdown, race prevention, and benchmark coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building a reliable concurrent processing component

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Go service for [requirements]. Cover APIs, data storage, security, observability, deployment, failure handling, profiling, and phased validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning an advanced service with operational requirements

output_examples.input: Review a worker pool that sometimes hangs during shutdown.
output: The review identifies blocked channel sends and incomplete cancellation propagation as the primary shutdown risks.
It proposes ownership rules for channel closure, context-aware workers, bounded queues, and timeout tests.
It recommends race detection and repeated stress tests before deployment.

output_examples.input: Plan performance work for a high-allocation HTTP service.
output: The plan starts with stable load benchmarks and CPU, heap, allocation, and trace profiles.
It ranks changes by measured impact, including buffer reuse, allocation reduction, connection tuning, and database query analysis.
It defines regression thresholds and compares results under representative traffic.

output_examples.input: Design a production gRPC service with graceful shutdown.
output: The design covers service boundaries, validation, authentication, deadlines, structured errors, health checks, metrics, and tracing.
Shutdown sequencing stops new traffic, drains active calls, closes dependencies, and enforces a final timeout.
The test strategy includes handler tests, integration tests, failure injection, and deployment readiness checks.

best_practices: Provide the Go version, repository context, workload, latency goals, and deployment constraints.
Request tests, benchmarks, and measurable acceptance criteria with every significant change.
Validate concurrency with cancellation tests, race detection, stress tests, and clear resource ownership.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize without benchmarks, profiles, traces, or representative production evidence.
Do not start goroutines without defined ownership, cancellation, error handling, and shutdown behavior.
Do not accept architecture advice without checking repository conventions and operational constraints.

faq.question: Which Go versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Go 1.21 and newer, with emphasis on modern language features, tooling, and standard library practices.

faq.question: Can it help with existing Go repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide relevant files, module details, constraints, and observed behavior for a grounded review.

faq.question: Does it support concurrency debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. It can analyze goroutine lifecycles, channels, synchronization, cancellation, races, deadlocks, and shutdown behavior.

faq.question: Can it guarantee performance improvements?
faq.answer: No. Performance claims require representative benchmarks, profiles, traces, and validation in the target environment.

faq.question: Can it design production microservices?
faq.answer: It can propose APIs, storage, reliability, observability, security, deployment, and testing strategies for Go services.

faq.question: Does it replace security or compliance review?
faq.answer: No. It provides secure coding guidance, but organization-specific controls and independent validation remain necessary.
